correctness.rationale: The support function is analytic with h+h''>3/4, proving a strictly convex body with perimeter 2pi. Reflection about axis beta sends each harmonic coefficient vector (a_m,b_m) to its Euclidean orthogonal projection onto angle m beta. The initial vector is aligned with axis zero; after any step it remains on one of the two projected axes, so each independent equiprobable next step multiplies the expected squared length by lambda_m=1-0.5 sin²(m alpha). Fourier orthogonality and area = (1/2) integral(h²-(h')²) give the exact positive convergent series for E D_t for all integers t>=0. For rational alpha/pi=p/q, lambda_m=1 exactly when q divides m; the rest has a uniform <1 bound on finitely many residue types. For irrational alpha/pi, every lambda_m<1 yet their supremum is 1 by density, yielding decay with no common exponential rate. For bounded continued-fraction coefficients, ||m alpha/pi||>=kappa/m yields upper exp(-c t^{1/3}) after optimizing 2sigma m+c t/m², and convergent denominators q_j comparable to t^{1/3} give a single-term matching lower bound. A new independent full two-axis projection-sequence test at finite t verified the harmonic conditional-energy formula; no finite test is used to prove the infinite decay bounds.

value.rationale: Two randomly selected fixed axes form a natural singular limit of random geometric symmetrization. The theorem displays a sharp arithmetic dynamical distinction: rational angles leave a positive area deficit, irrational ones round without a uniform exponential rate, and badly approximable irrational angles have stretched-exponential exponent 1/3 for a smooth explicit body. This precise structural rate boundary motivates the specific observable and source class; it is not merely a numerical illustration.
